title: Let /review-code review a candidate commit (its diff against a recorded base), not only working-tree changes
outcome: Let /review-code review a candidate commit (its diff against a recorded base), not only working-tree changes
acceptance: Both /review-changes and /review-code accept an explicitly supplied candidate commit and recorded base commit as the review target, inspect the complete BASE-to-COMMIT change including added and deleted files, and do not stop merely because the candidate checkout is clean; without a supplied commit target, the existing staged, unstaged and untracked workflow remains available.

The parent records the resolved base commit, candidate commit and candidate tree id on the item and in each reviewer's multiline brief; committed-input reviews verify the expected HEAD, tree and clean tracked/index/untracked state independently at start and end, and missing or invalid identities, a dirty candidate checkout or an identity mismatch are reported explicitly rather than treated as a clean review.

The candidate workflow requires the existing maintained gate on the same unchanged recorded candidate commit only once, without a mandatory working-tree gate followed by a second candidate gate; the current staged-input gate path, failed-gate investigation and changed-input revalidation requirements remain unchanged.

The change reuses Engram's existing committed-input and F1 target-selection wording where applicable, cites both CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md when referring to the standing rule, and grants no new commit, push, install, restart, review-reuse or test-ref exception; any authority-sensitive instruction wording completes the required instruction-change process before landing.

Validation covers a clean recorded commit with a nonempty base diff, added/deleted-file inventory, missing or invalid target identity, dirty committed input, and the existing no-commit-target path, using bounded read-only Git examples and independent review; evidence identifies the exact instruction revision and its limits.
